extracted.intended_audience: household cooks / domestic cooks seeking recipes and preserving guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical domestic-cookbook instructions for making breads, cakes, ice-creams, preserves, pickles, and related dishes, plus general tips for equipment and storage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bread flour weight
rubrics_metrics.description: A quart of flour should weigh just one pound and a quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this weight as a standard when measuring by volume for consistent dough. (Context: general bread recipes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rasp bread when baked
rubrics_metrics.description: The bread must be rasped when baked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finish bread with a rasping action after baking — instruction given as a necessary finishing step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for making bread by season
rubrics_metrics.description: In winter, make the bread up at three o'clock so it will be ready before bed; in summer, make it up at five o'clock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust dough preparation time based on ambient temperature to ensure proper rising before use.

rubrics_metrics.name: To make nice biscuit
rubrics_metrics.description: Rub a large spoonful of butter into a quart of risen dough, knead well, form into biscuit (thick or thin), and bake quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick baking after shaping is emphasized; proportion of butter (large spoonful per quart dough) provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rice bread proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil six ounces of rice in a quart of water until dry and soft; put into two pounds of flour, add two teaspoons salt, two large spoonsful yeast, and enough water to make bread consistency; when risen, bake in moulds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cooked rice to enrich dough; bake in moulds once risen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed bread with gruel
rubrics_metrics.description: Put a teaspoonful of salt and a large one of yeast into a quart of flour; make soft with corn meal gruel; when well risen, bake in a mould.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indifferent flour rises better with gruel than with water; recommended for breakfast bread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent yeast (hop-based) preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil half a pound of fresh hops in a gallon of water down to two quarts; strain, make a thin batter with flour, add half a pint good yeast, ferment, work in corn meal to biscuit consistency, let rise, form cakes and dry in shade; keep dry and protected from damp and dust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative: use brewer's yeast (one quart brewer's yeast + one quart water) to save trouble. Dry cakes in shade, turn frequently; store securely to prevent damp/dust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing yeast cakes for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissolve one or more yeast cakes in a little warm water, stir, thicken with a little flour, set near the fire to rise before using.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best container is a small mug or pitcher with close stopper and double fold of linen under stopper — preferable to a bottle and easier to clean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative yeast from potato
rubrics_metrics.description: Peel and boil one large Irish potato, sieve it, add equal quantity of flour, dilute with hop tea; when a little warmer than new milk add a gill of good yeast, stir and keep covered in a small pitcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potato-based yeast as another method; keep closely covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nice buns
rubrics_metrics.description: Four ounces sugar with 3/4 lb flour, 2 spoonsful yeast, 1/2 pint milk; when risen, work in 4 oz butter, shape small buns, bake in quick oven — do not burn them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against burning; quick oven recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muffins method
rubrics_metrics.description: Sift a quart of flour, add a little salt and a large spoonful of yeast; beat white of fresh egg to strong froth, add and make up with cold water as soft as handled; set in moderately warm place, next morning beat, cook on griddle in round form, turn frequently until done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overnight fermentation; use egg white froth for lightness; turn frequently on griddle.

rubrics_metrics.name: French rolls
rubrics_metrics.description: Sift a quart of flour, add a little salt, a spoonful of yeast, two beaten eggs and 1/2 pint milk; knead, let rise; next morning work in ounce of butter, form small rolls and bake. The top crust should not be hard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages a tender top crust — avoid hard crust on top.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crumpets preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a quart dough early morning, separate egg yolks and whites, whip both to froth, mix with dough, add milk-warm water gradually to batter thickness like buckwheat cakes; set to rise until near breakfast; pour on griddle to form round — they do not require turning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not turn crumpets on griddle; consistency and rise time emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apoquiniminc cakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Quart of flour with a little salt, one beaten egg, 4 oz butter; make paste with new milk, beat half an hour with pestle, roll thin, cut round and bake on gridiron — be careful not to burn them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long beating and thin rolling; avoid burning on gridiron.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batter cakes with yeast substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil two cups small homony very soft, add equal corn meal with salt and large spoonful butter; make thin batter with three eggs and milk, beat, bake on griddle or waffle irons. When eggs not available, use a spoonful of yeast and let stand an hour to rise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yeast can substitute eggs; batter should be beaten till light.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batter bread
rubrics_metrics.description: Six spoonfuls flour and three corn meal with salt; make thin batter with four eggs and sufficient rich milk; bake in little tin moulds in quick oven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small tin moulds and quick oven recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cream cakes and Soufflé biscuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Cream cakes: melt butter in a pint of milk to make rich as cream, make flour into paste, knead, roll, cut and bake on griddle. Soufflé biscuits: rub 4 oz butter into quart flour, make paste with milk, knead, roll as thin as paper, bake to look white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roll thin; for soufflé biscuits avoid browning — keep them white-looking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corn meal bread
rubrics_metrics.description: Rub butter size of an egg into a pint corn meal; make batter with two eggs and new milk; add a spoonful yeast, set by the fire an hour to rise, butter little pans and bake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use yeast and short rise; butter pans for baking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sweet potato buns
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil and mash a potato, rub in flour to make like bread; add spice and sugar to taste, spoonful yeast; when risen work in butter and bake in small rolls to be eaten hot with butter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve hot; use yeast for rise; season to taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rice waffles / woffles
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil two gills rice soft, mix with three gills flour, salt, 2 oz melted butter, 2 eggs, milk to thick batter; beat till very light and bake in waffle irons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beat batter until very light before cooking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buckwheat cakes caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix a large spoonful yeast and a little salt into a quart buckwheat meal with cold water; let rise well and bake on griddle — it turns sour quickly if allowed to stand any time after it has risen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use promptly after rise; do not let buckwheat batter stand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ice-cream freezer construction & operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Freezer should be 12–14 inches deep and 8–10 inches wide to give larger surface for ice formation on sides; use a silver long-handled spoon to scrape ice from sides as it forms; keep freezer constantly in motion; use pewter freezers rather than tin to avoid wear and saltwater ingress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large surface area speeds freezing; constant motion and scraping encouraged; pewter preferred to tin to avoid holes and saltwater contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freezer-in-tub anti-pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting the freezer in a tub with ice and salt and putting it in the ice house will freeze but watery particles will subside and destroy the cream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not freeze by simply leaving freezer in ice house; this causes separation and inferior texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packing and setting ice cream in moulds
rubrics_metrics.description: When congealed, pack in moulds placed upright and keep in ice and salt until sufficiently hard; do not turn out until moment of serving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place moulds upright; leave in ice/salt until firm; unmould just before serving to retain shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ice-cream freezing vessel fit in tub
rubrics_metrics.description: Freezing tub must be wide enough to leave a margin of 4–5 inches all around the freezer when placed in the middle — otherwise a larger tub wastes ice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize tub-to-freezer fit to minimize ice usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve non-shaped ice-creams in handled glasses
rubrics_metrics.description: When ice creams are not put into shapes, they should always be served in glasses with handles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation tip for un-moulded ice cream.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanilla cream sugar adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil a vanilla bean in a quart of rich milk, remove bean, mix with the milk eight eggs beaten; let it boil a little longer and make it very sweet because much sugar is lost in freezing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensate for sugar loss during freezing by making custard quite sweet initially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fruit cream using custard when cream unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: Raspberry and strawberry creams: make a quart of rich boiled custard, when cold pour on a quart of ripe fruit, mash, sieve, sweeten, and freeze. Rich cream is superior — custard is a substitute when cream cannot be had.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fully ripe fruit; custard is acceptable substitute but fresh cream is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cocoa nut cream ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Grate a coconut fine and mix with a quart of cream; sweeten and freeze — small nuts require 1.5 to flavor a quart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust quantity of nut to strength of flavor desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chocolate cream technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Scrape 1/4 lb chocolate fine, boil in quart of milk stirring continually, thicken with six eggs; adding a vanilla bean improves flavor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constant stirring while dissolving chocolate and using eggs to thicken; vanilla recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coffee cream toasting coffee
rubrics_metrics.description: Toast two gills of raw coffee till light brown but not burnt; put hot from toaster into quart rich sweet milk, boil, add yolks of eight eggs, strain and sweeten; if done properly it will not be discoloured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Toast coffee carefully (no burning); avoid grinding before adding to milk; strain to prevent discoloration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemon cream care to avoid curdling
rubrics_metrics.description: Pare yellow rind thin from four lemons, boil in quart fresh cream, squeeze and strain juice of one lemon, saturate with powdered sugar, stir into cold cream — take care it does not curdle; if not sufficiently sweet add more sugar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid curdling by controlling temperature when adding citrus. Adjust sweetness after combining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemonade iced with whipped egg whites
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a quart of rich lemonade, whip whites of six eggs to strong froth, mix with lemonade and freeze.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use egg white foam to lighten iced lemonade; analogous methods for cherry or currant ices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custard baking in water bath (Dutch oven)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a quart of milk quite hot, let get cold, mix six eggs, sweeten with loaf sugar, fill custard cups, set in Dutch oven with water (not so much as to risk boiling into cups), do not put on top of oven; when water has boiled 10–15 minutes test one cup — if custard is jelly-like it is done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use moderate heat and water bath to prevent whey separation; test consistency before removing; serve with covers on and grate nutmeg when cold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trifle assembly standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Put slices of Savoy cake or Naples biscuit at bottom of deep dish, wet with white wine, fill nearly to top with rich boiled custard; whip cream seasoned with white wine and sugar and lay lightly on top; pile high and decorate with thin-cut preserves so as not to weigh down froth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve slices should be cut thin to avoid collapsing whipped cream; presentation and layering emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blanc mange composition and colour guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 1 oz isinglass soaked then boiled, add a quart milk, boil till dissolved, strain, add 2 oz sweet almonds pounded, sweeten and mould. For colouring moulds (ear of corn, asparagus, etc.) use egg yelk or spinach juice; fruit should be the natural colour; cochineal and alkanet root in brandy make good colouring; always serve blanc mange with raspberry cream or syllabub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour fruit & decorative moulds carefully using natural-appearing colours; always accompany with a sauce (raspberry cream or syllabub).

rubrics_metrics.name: Making slip (rennet curd) timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a quart rich milk moderately warm, stir in one large spoonful of prepared rennet, set by; when cold it will be as stiff as jelly. It should be made only a few hours before use or it will be tough and watery; in summer set dish in ice after jellied and eat with powdered sugar, cream, and nutmeg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing crucial: use within few hours; in summer cool in ice to preserve texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curds and cream serving
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn one quart milk as for slip, let stand until just before serving, take curds up with skimming dish and drain on sieve; surround with cream, use sugar and nutmeg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let curds drain too long; serve immediately with cream.

rubrics_metrics.name: Savoury jelly preparation (clarification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil 8–10 lb coarse lean beef or similar veal parts in 2 gallons water with 1 lb lean salt pork, onions, carrots, parsley and sweet herbs until reduced to 2 quarts; strain next day, remove fat and dregs; reheat with 1/2 pint white wine, spoonful lemon pickle, whites & shells of 4 eggs beaten; when boils clear on one side run through jelly bag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use egg whites and shells for clarification; cool and remove fat before final clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-la-daub (meat aspic) assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Roast birds, lay on set jelly with breasts down in deep dish, fill dish with jelly up to backs while jelly is cold, and just before serving loosen in hot water and turn out carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure jelly is not warm enough to melt previous layer; chill fully before filling; serve by briefly loosening in warm water.

rubrics_metrics.name: General directions for making preserves (equipment & process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserving pan: bell metal, flat bottom, very large diameter but not deep, close-fitting cover and side handles. Also have a large chafing-dish with long legs; a pierced ladle with long handle for removing fruit without syrup. Use best double-refined sugar or amber sugar-house syrup if available (less fermentation). Delicate fruit should be done gently and not remain more than half an hour after it begins to stew before cooling and repeating in syrup until transparent. Do not put more in pan than can lie on bottom without crowding. Keep pan bright and do not permit anything to cool in it (else it cankers). Store delicate preserves in small glasses/pots (1–2 lb) because admission of air injures them; put wet letter paper with brandy on preserves and cover with many folds of soft paper; keep in dry place and expose constantly to sun to check fermentation. Fruit for preserving should be in full perfection but not too ripe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long, detailed equipment and process guidance: pan choice, sugar quality, gentle handling for delicate fruit, cooling cycles (take out to cool and return to syrup repeatedly until clear), avoid crowding, cleanliness, small storage containers, use brandy-wet paper seals, sun exposure to prevent fermentation, and fruit ripeness advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peach preserving (cling-stone) method
rubrics_metrics.description: Use finest yellow cling-stones, pare and lay in bowl; sprinkle their weight in pounded sugar as added, let stand 2–3 hours, then put sugar+fruit into pan with little water, scald till thoroughly scalded, remove with ladle draining syrup; if not enough syrup add water, boil and skim then return fruit and do gently till clear. Blanch and preserve kernels with peaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sugar-to-fruit weight and initial maceration recommended; scald gently and skim; save and use kernels for flavor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currant jelly best-practice (no pressing for best jelly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick full ripe currants, set stoneware pot in iron pot of water to extract juice (no water getting in), pour into jelly bag and let run as long as it will without pressing — reserve pressed liquor for inferior jelly. To each pint of this juice add 1 pound powdered loaf sugar and boil 15–20 minutes, skim clean and put in glasses; expose daily to sun to prevent fermentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not press for best quality; reserved pressed juice for inferior jelly; daily sun exposure to avoid fermentation; sugar proportion 1 lb per pint juice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quince jelly and marmalade procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Quinces: choose perfect fruit, let them yellow and fragrant, scald, pare and stew in sugar syrup equal to weight of quinces; for jelly: stew quinces, pass through jelly bag and do not press for best jelly — to each pint of juice add 1 lb powdered loaf sugar and boil to jelly. For marmalade: boil quinces, cool, rub pulp through sieve, mix 2 lb pulp to 1 lb sugar, sift pounded cochineal for colour, tie seeds in muslin bag and boil with marmalade, remove seeds and pot when thick.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate jelly (no pressing) vs inferior (pressing allowed); marmalade uses pulp-to-sugar ratios and colouring guidance (cochineal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cherries preserving guidance (stem, clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select carnation and common light red cherries with short stems and not too ripe; use equal weight of double-refined sugar to cherries, make syrup and preserve without stoning and with stems on; if done carefully stems won't come off and fruit will be transparent so stones are visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve cherries whole with stems to improve appearance and transparency; use equal-weight sugar syrup and careful handling to avoid stem loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drying cherries
rubrics_metrics.description: Stone cherries and save juice; weigh cherries and allow 1 lb good brown sugar to 3 lb fruit; boil with juice, stew 15–20 minutes, drain syrup and dry cherries in sun turning frequently, sprinkling powdered loaf sugar between layers when packing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save and reuse syrup; frequent turning while sun-drying; powdered sugar between layers for preservation; leftover syrup used on more fruit until exhausted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tomato catsup and soy processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Tomato catsup: boil picked tomatoes without water for an hour with a few spoons salt, strain, then boil with chopped onions, mace, pepper and additional salt until just enough to fill two bottles; cork tightly. Tomato soy: salt-layer sliced ripe tomatoes in tub with onions and 1/2 pint salt over each ~2-inch layer; after 3 days boil mixture from early morning till night stirring constantly; next morning pass through sieve pressing for liquor, add cloves, allspice, black pepper and small wine glass of Cayenne, boil slowly all day, cool, bottle and cork, store cool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catsup: make in dry weather (August). Soy: lengthy continuous boiling and seasoning; emphasize careful long boiling and proper bottling and cool storage to preserve.
